key_insight: A finite spanwise-oscillating wall achieves 32% drag reduction, with skin-friction onset and recovery following exponential responses over length scales of 0.6δ and 0.9δ, respectively.
engineering_relevance: These response lengths can inform the placement and sizing of finite wall-actuation patches for turbulent boundary-layer drag control.
method: Investigate a turbulent boundary layer at Reτ = 652 with oscillation period T+ ≈ 101 and amplitude A+ ≈ 7.
Estimate local skin friction using arctangent-based nonlinear regression of near-wall data.
Track turbulence statistics and conditional quadrant events across actuation onset and recovery.
evidence_signal: The skin-friction method was assessed against reference DNS data and reproduced experimental measurement-error trends; most Reynolds-stress responses had fitted length scales within 0.5δ, except the slower shear-stress peak.
watch_item: The reported performance is for one Reynolds number and actuation setting; net energy savings cannot be inferred without actuation-power data.
paper_title: Spatially developing drag reduction across a finite oscillating wall
